name: 240 Turbo Evolution
hook: Volvo lined up five hundred race-ready Evolution cars in America for the inspectors, and by one account only twenty-three of them were the real thing.
story:
Picture two fields in America, July 1983. One on the west coast, one on the east. Five hundred boxy Volvos sit in neat rows.

The rules say a racing special needs five hundred road-going twins. So here they are. Bigger turbo. A new rear spoiler. And a trick Volvo invented and patented: water sprayed into the intake to cool the air. Volvo calls it Water Turbo Traction.

The inspectors look, and they sign.

Now the story goes sideways. One account says only twenty-three cars were true Evolutions. The rest lost their special parts and were sold as plain 240 Turbos. Later, the governing body tried to buy an Evolution and asked for the owners' names. Volvo could not produce them.

By then it hardly mattered on track. In 1985 the brick flew. Thomas Lindström and Gianfranco Brancatelli won the European Touring Car Championship for the Eggenberger team. Six wins from fourteen races, in a car shaped like a fridge.
description: The 240 Turbo Evolution was Volvo's Group A homologation special. Group A demanded 500 examples of an evolution model, so Volvo built them and had them inspected in the United States in July 1983. They carried a larger turbo, recalibrated engine control, water injection and a rear spoiler. Race versions made about 300 hp from the 2.1-litre four. Run by Eggenberger, the car won the 1985 European Touring Car Championship, and how many genuine Evolutions reached customers is still argued over.
